title: $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ is profinite
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with a set of objects and a set of morphisms between each pair of objects, and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathbf{Sets}$ be a functor. Regard each $F(X)$ as a discrete space, give $\operatorname{Aut}(F(X))$ the compact-open topology (equivalently, the topology of pointwise convergence), and give $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ the topology induced by evaluation into the product. Then evaluation identifies $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ with a closed subgroup of $\prod_X\operatorname{Aut}(F(X))$. Consequently, if all $F(X)$ are finite, then $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ is profinite.

proof.text: Evaluation sends a natural automorphism $a$ to the family $(a_X)_X$ of bijections of $F(X)$, and is an injective group homomorphism because a natural transformation is determined by its components. Conversely, a family $(\gamma_X)_X$ of bijections is in its image exactly when $F(f)\circ\gamma_X=\gamma_{X'}\circ F(f)$ for every arrow $f:X\to X'$; these equalities give a natural isomorphism whose inverse has components $\gamma_X^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0BMR, lemma-aut-inverse-limit, first two sentences of proof; section-galois, equation-embedding-product

proof.text: Express the evaluation image, using step 1, as the intersection over every arrow f : X → Y and every x ∈ F(X) of the equalizer of the two maps a ↦ F(f)(a_X(x)) and a ↦ a_Y(F(f)(x)). Both maps are continuous into the discrete Hausdorff space F(Y): component projection, permutation evaluation at a fixed point, and any map between discrete spaces are continuous. Each equalizer is closed by isClosed_eq, and their intersection is closed by isClosed_iInter. Together with the induced topology and the injectivity from step 1 this gives an IsClosedEmbedding. This equalizer formulation also covers X = Y without separating the two projections.

For finite fibres, the function space F(X) → F(X) is finite and discrete. The injective hom-component map from Aut(F(X)) into this function space induces the stipulated pointwise topology, hence its source is finite and discrete as well. The product of these groups is compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected and a topological group, as in lem-galois-closed-subgroup-product-finite-groups. Transfer compactness via IsClosedEmbedding.compactSpace, Hausdorffness via T2Space.of_injective_continuous, and total disconnectedness via IsEmbedding.isTotallyDisconnected_range. Transfer continuous multiplication and inversion via IsInducing.continuousMul and IsInducing.continuousInv applied to the evaluation monoid homomorphism. This yields all four asserted structures on Aut(F).
